name: FedEx
key_signal: Stock is up 24.8% over 126 days and remains above both moving averages (golden cross intact), but short-term momentum has turned negative (-6.4% in 21 days, MACD histogram negative, price below 50-day SMA) as it consolidates near the top of its 52-week range.
thesis: FedEx trades at a modest 15.3x forward earnings despite 12.5% revenue growth, an 11.1% operating margin, and 14.8% ROE, reflecting ongoing network optimization (DRIVE program) benefits. The stock's longer-term trend remains firmly bullish—up 25% over six months, above its 200-day SMA with a golden cross intact—suggesting institutional accumulation and confidence in margin recovery post-restructuring. A 1.56% dividend yield and buy-rated consensus among 25 analysts add support, and free cash flow of $5.5B gives management flexibility for buybacks/debt reduction even with elevated debt-to-equity of 136%.
bear_case: Earnings growth is actually negative (-4.6%) despite revenue growth of 12.5%, indicating margin pressure or one-time cost drags that the market may be underestimating, and the recent price action—a 6.4% pullback over the last month, RSI at 46, negative MACD histogram, and price falling below the 50-day SMA—suggests the momentum-driven run to $345 has stalled and could reverse further, especially given a high beta of 1.34 in a slowing freight/industrial demand environment where FedEx's premium express/ground volumes are cyclically exposed.
